newsitem.title: USA: Putnam Website to allow planners to open accounts.
newsitem.headline: Putnam Website to allow planners to open accounts.

text.p: Putnam Investments said it will upgraded its Website to permit financial planners to open accounts and trade mutual funds over the Internet.
"Putnam is really the first company able to do this," Mark McKenna, director of communications, told Reuters in an interview.

The mutual fund company also began delivering quarterly statements to its financial advisers and back-office firms on CD-ROMs rather than paper, greatly cutting down the amount of work, said Gavan Taylor, Putnam's chief information officer.
Putnam currently sends out around 4.8 million pieces of paper each quarter to the more than 80,000 brokers who sell Putnam funds, but the CD-ROMs will save paperwork, Taylor said.

Also on the Website, financial advisors and retirement plan sponsors will be able to check their clients' statements, fund performance figures, asset allocation strategies, demographic information about plan participants and other information.
Individual investors will also be able to access the Putnamwebsite (www.putnaminv.com) and access daily account information and consult asset allocation charts and educational materials, Putnam said.
Financial planners and investers will also be able to send e-mail to Putnam and any questions they may have, Taylor said.
The Website, which has had 350,000 hits since its launch last September, will gradually be upgraded over the year to include the additional services, he said.
"Our plan is by the end of the year to have the most comprehensive program offered," Taylor said.
